correctness.rationale: At \(\mathcal R_0=1\), the exact infected equation plus the source monotonicity hypotheses gives \(I'\le-\beta_\star I^2\). This proves extinction and an \(O(t^{-1})\) bound. The \(H\), \(R\), and population-deficit equations are stable linear filters, giving full-state convergence and ratio limits. Differentiability of \(f(N)=\beta(N)N\) then gives \(I'/I^2\to-K\), proving the exact vector profile and logarithmic integral laws. The numerical replay is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The equality boundary is the transition between eradication and endemicity. The result shows it is qualitatively different from the strict subcritical regime: infection decays only as \(t^{-1}\), hospital and recovery loads inherit explicit proportional tails, and cumulative infection and confirmation grow logarithmically. The coefficient \(K\) separates direct depletion, downstream residence, disease-induced population deficit, and contact-law slope, making it a motivated critical invariant rather than a cosmetic endpoint extension.
